purpose: Review a newly accessible Batanes common-dolphinfish stock assessment as single-taxon fishery evidence, separate landing centers from capture grounds, and retain the study's mixed stock indicators without presenting them as current fishing or conservation advice.

source.title: Stock Status of Coryphaena hippurus (Common Dolphinfish) in Fisheries Management Area 1, Batanes Waters Sub-FMA
source.publisher: The Philippine Journal of Fisheries; National Fisheries Research and Development Institute
source.license: CC BY-NC 4.0, as stated on the article's final page.
source.access: Official NFRDI-hosted full article PDF opened and reviewed; no local copy retained.

study.waterbodyOrManagementArea: Batanes Waters sub-FMA within Fisheries Management Area 1; this is the article's fishery-management scope, not a surveyed point or resolved habitat polygon.
study.samplingUnit: Coryphaena hippurus landed catch recorded by NSAP enumerators at established landing sites; this is fishery-dependent evidence, not a direct fish-community survey.
study.dataCollection: The article says data were gathered at established landing sites under standard NSAP methodology, then submitted to BFAR Region 02 for evaluation, encoding, and analysis. Fork length was used for length-frequency records.
study.populationParameterSubset: FiSAT population parameters were computed only from 2022–2023 length frequencies and only from troll-line catch, because earlier years lacked sufficient length-frequency records for the software and troll line supplied the complete usable length set.
spatialLimits: Municipality and landing-site labels identify where landings were recorded, not where fish were caught.
The article's overview map depicts landing markers but supplies no verified coordinate table or fishery-event-to-capture-ground crosswalk; no points or fishing-ground geometry were derived.
The study supports a Batanes fishery-level historical source lead, not local residency or site-specific occurrence at every landing center.

reportedFindings.catchTrendInterpretation: The abstract describes historical catch and CPUE as increasing overall, while the results describe fluctuations and declines in 2016 and 2020 during the 2014–2023 series. The article attributes most catch to troll line and explicitly says the localized, selective gear and data focus complicate interpretation.

assessmentLimits: The paper's indicators do not give a single unqualified stock conclusion: FiSAT estimates E=0.85 and high fishing mortality from troll-line length data, while CMSY and the reported SPR metrics indicate healthy biomass/reproductive status. The article itself discusses this disparity and cautions against increasing fishing capacity.

The 2022–2023 FiSAT subset is not the full 2014–2023 catch series and covers only troll-line lengths; do not generalize these estimates to every gear or the full migratory stock without qualification.

The article does not publish the underlying catch dataset, individual fish records, specimen vouchers, capture coordinates, effort by each capture ground, or a landing-to-capture-area matrix in the reviewed text.

The source's historical CPUE, mortality, exploitation, SPR, and CMSY estimates are study results, not current conservation status, legal rules, safety advice, abundance at a specific location, bait guidance, or guaranteed catchability.
CC BY-NC 4.0 permits noncommercial reuse with attribution; no article figure, table, map, or adapted content was copied. Product publication approval remains false.
nextAction: Seek a public or author-approved catch extract with annual gear-specific effort, landing-site totals, capture-ground descriptions, and data definitions. Keep any such fishery data separate from biodiversity occurrences and verify current licensing and management sources before app use.
